Jordan —

Appreciate the quick read. I’m copying Laura (legal) and Ben (AM) to coordinate. Two quick asks from our side:

- We generally standardize on a 30/60/90 cadence depending on contract value; can you confirm the procurement policy is a hard 60 days? We can propose a 45‑day compromise if that helps move it.
- On TFC during the first 90 days: we’re open to a time‑boxed carveout but typically cap TFC liability (termination fee) to the remainder of prepaid fees or a fixed % of ARR for short windows.

Laura — can you propose redline language that (a) accepts a 60‑day notice or proposes 45 days as compromise and (b) limits the early TFC to a fixed fee no greater than 10% of the first year’s committed ARR or remaining prepaid MRC? If you prefer, we can also offer a sunrise exemption that prevents auto‑renew for that first 90 days with a short notice process.

Jordan — once Laura sends suggested language, we’ll route to procurement/legal and aim to get DocuSign link by EOD 11/25.

Jordan / team —

Thanks for the redline, Jordan. I reviewed and drafted two narrow options in the attached MSA redline (Redwood_MSA_Term_V4_redline.pdf):

Option A (Procurement box):
- Notice: Acceptable to move to 60 days if the customer commits to an annual term and prepayment; otherwise we propose 45 days.
- TFC (first 90 days): Customer may terminate for convenience within first 90 days; Redwood’s sole remedy is a termination fee equal to the lesser of (i) remaining prepaid fees, or (ii) 10% of committed ARR for year 1.

Option B (Sunrise exemption):
- Prevent auto‑renewal for the first 90 days post‑execution (no rollover clock). After day 90, standard auto‑renew applies with 30‑day non‑renewal notice unless otherwise agreed.

Rationale: Option A preserves Redwood’s pricing predictability while giving procurement the 60‑day visibility; Option B avoids an early auto‑renewal trap for Acme during integration. Either option is acceptable to us, we recommend Option A for larger committed deals and Option B for pilots.

I also inserted explicit notice mechanics (sent to contractual billing and legal emails) and a small admin fee for early TFC to discourage gaming. See attached for exact redline text.

If that aligns, Ben — please confirm commercial tradeoffs (45 vs 60 and whether we accept 10% cap) so I can finalize for signature.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
